fields.sections.1.h: Recent Incident Response and Security Control Status

fields.sections.3.h: Social Media Expansion and Strategic Reassessment
fields.sections.4.h: Customer Support and Service Continuity During Transition
fields.sections.5.h: Independence Assurance of Other Business Divisions
fields.sections.6.h: Company's Global Position and Business Portfolio
fields.sections.0.ko: India's digital trust services company eMudhra has decided to completely exit the global SSL/TLS certificate business through a board decision in October 2026. This is not merely a business restructuring but represents a determination to shift the company's strategic focus toward enterprise solutions and trust services beyond SSL/TLS.
fields.sections.1.ko: Chairman V. Srinivasan mentioned a recent SSL/TLS certificate-related incident, explaining that eMudhra revoked the affected Certificate Authority (CA) within 14 hours of discovery and disclosed it promptly. He emphasized that no end-user certificates were issued, there was no infrastructure compromise or data breach, and both physical and logical security controls remained intact.
fields.sections.2.ko: The SSL/TLS business represents less than approximately 1% of eMudhra's global revenue, a small segment. However, over time, compliance requirements for data sovereignty regulations have increased, with accumulated complexity and costs. Simultaneously, large platform companies have begun providing SSL/TLS for free, causing the business's growth potential and return on investment to decrease significantly relative to the company's overall scale.
fields.sections.3.ko: The recent incident became excessively amplified on social media, concentrating disproportionate attention and criticism on the company as a whole. After intensive review, the board determined that withdrawal from SSL/TLS is in the best interest of eMudhra and its shareholders. It noted that while SSL/TLS is a core business for most certificate authorities, for eMudhra it is merely one part of a broad digital solutions portfolio.
fields.sections.4.ko: The G1 RSA root certificate will continue to be serviced for customers until the transition is complete, and eMudhra will proceed through collaboration with browser programs and customers. Affected customers will receive free certificate replacement through partners, and the company plans to operate revocation and certificate status services until all issued certificates expire or are replaced.
fields.sections.5.ko: eMudhra's global SSL/TLS infrastructure is completely separated from the company's other operations. Therefore, core services including digital signature certificates, eSign, signature services within India, enterprise PKI solutions (emCA, CertiNext platform), emSigner electronic signature suite, and identity and authentication solutions (SecurePass, emAS) will all continue to operate normally.
fields.sections.6.ko: Based on more than 17 years of experience, eMudhra is a global company that has supplied digital identity, trust, and security solutions to financial, government, and enterprise customers in over 35 countries. Through product lines such as CertiNext (PKI and certificate lifecycle management), SecurePass (identity and access management, multi-factor authentication), and PrivaTrust (data discovery and regulatory compliance consent management), the company provides high-trust digital services at population scale.
fields.caveat: This press release represents eMudhra's official position; independent verification of the technical impact of the incident and changes in industry trust levels is necessary.
